title: How often: mindig, gyakran, általában, néha, ritkán

sections.content: Hungarian has five small words for how often you do something. They are adverbs, so they never change. Put one right before the verb: *Mindig olvasok.* means “I always read.” The verb ending already says who acts, so *én* stays out.

sections.title: With a time word
sections.content: A time word can come first, and then the frequency word follows it: *Reggel mindig olvasok.* (In the morning I always read.) Both go before the verb.

items.english: At noon we usually have lunch.

sections.content: English can say “I read often” or “Often I read”. In Hungarian, start with the frequency word right before the verb: *Gyakran olvasok.* Do not add *én*; *Én gyakran olvasok* sounds like “I do, but others do not.”
